answer: An agent registry can resist Sybil swarms with a max-flow endorsement graph rooted in an audited seed kernel. Agents sign capacity-capped vouches for trusted peers, and verifiers admit keys receiving threshold flow from it. Because min-cut bounds cap total incoming flow, an attacker's Sybil island cannot sustain a plume of accepted keys without buying or earning scarce cross-cut vouches per identity. Still, peripheral newcomers risk exclusion, and colluding seeds can admit fakes.
